articles.original_title: Statement from Canada on the participation of Russian and Belarusian athletes in international sport
articles.original_summary: The Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs; the Honourable, Lena Metlege Diab, Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship; and the Honourable Adam van Koeverden, Secretary of State (Sport), issued the following statement: “Since Russia’s full-scale and illegal invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Canada has stood firmly with the people of Ukraine, committing more than $26 billion in assistance and imposing sanctions on more than 4,200 individuals, entities and vessels. As part of this broader response, Canada has also consistently opposed the participation of athletes representing Russia and Belarus under their national flags, symbols, colours or anthems in international sporting competitions. This opposition will continue.

articles.original_title: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework
articles.original_summary: The Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada jointly review and renew the Bank’s monetary policy framework every five years. The Bank then independently conducts monetary policy to achieve the framework’s goals. The Government and the Bank agree that monetary policy must work to promote the economic and financial well being of Canadians. We also agree that the best way monetary policy can do this is by keeping inflation low, stable, and predictable, thereby protecting Canadians from large increases in the cost of living. A credible and well understood monetary policy framework that focuses on price stability helps the economy grow, supports investment and job creation, and fosters confidence in Canada’s economy.

articles.original_title: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework
articles.original_summary: The Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada jointly review and renew the Bank’s monetary policy framework every five years. The Bank then independently conducts monetary policy to achieve the framework’s goals. The Government and the Bank agree that monetary policy must work to promote the economic and financial well being of Canadians. We also agree that the best way monetary policy can do this is by keeping inflation low, stable, and predictable, thereby protecting Canadians from large increases in the cost of living. A credible and well understood monetary policy framework that focuses on price stability helps the economy grow, supports investment and job creation, and fosters confidence in Canada’s economy.

articles.original_title: Statement from Canada on the participation of Russian and Belarusian athletes in international sport
articles.original_summary: The Honourable Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs; the Honourable, Lena Metlege Diab, Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship; and the Honourable Adam van Koeverden, Secretary of State (Sport), issued the following statement: “Since Russia’s full-scale and illegal invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Canada has stood firmly with the people of Ukraine, committing more than $26 billion in assistance and imposing sanctions on more than 4,200 individuals, entities and vessels. As part of this broader response, Canada has also consistently opposed the participation of athletes representing Russia and Belarus under their national flags, symbols, colours or anthems in international sporting competitions. This opposition will continue.

articles.original_title: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework
articles.original_summary: The Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada jointly review and renew the Bank’s monetary policy framework every five years. The Bank then independently conducts monetary policy to achieve the framework’s goals. The Government and the Bank agree that monetary policy must work to promote the economic and financial well being of Canadians. We also agree that the best way monetary policy can do this is by keeping inflation low, stable, and predictable, thereby protecting Canadians from large increases in the cost of living. A credible and well understood monetary policy framework that focuses on price stability helps the economy grow, supports investment and job creation, and fosters confidence in Canada’s economy.
